overview.description: Illustrated Tarokk (Illusztrált Tarokk) is the most complex and rewarding variant of Hungarian Tarokk. While based on the 42-card 'Twenty-Calling' (Paskievics) version, it adds a massive layer of additional bonuses (Figurák) that make it a game of high-stakes declarations and daring tactical plays. In this variant, winning the basic game is often secondary to fulfilling high-value bonus contracts like 'Huszonegyfogás' (Catching the XXI).

history.origins: Developed in the late 19th and early 20th centuries as Hungarian players sought to add more tactical variety to the traditional Paskievics-tarokk. It became the 'Illustrated' version because of the numerous 'figures' (bonuses) that decorate the scoring sheet.
timeline: 1900-1920: Scoring bonuses like 'Uhu' and 'Kismadár' are added to the basic game.
1950s: Rules are standardized for tournament play.
Present: The standard variant for serious competitive Hungarian Tarokk players.
history.evolution: The game shifted focus toward anticipating and declaring bonuses. A player receiving a powerful hand doesn't just try to win; they try to 'illustrate' their hand by declaring as many bonuses as possible.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'Queen of Games' in Hungary; requires deep focus and partnership intuition.

setup.players: 4 players in hidden partnerships (established by calling the XX).
setup.deck: 42-card Tarot pack. Ranking: Skíz (highest), XXI, XX... I (Pagát).
setup.dealing: Same as Húszashívásos Tarokk (6 in talon, hands of 9 cards).

rules.objective: Win at least 48 points and fulfill declared bonuses for maximum points.
rules.gameplay: Standard Tarokk rules apply: Must follow suit, must trump if unable, partnership established by calling the XX.
keyRules: Follow suit; if void in suit led, must play a tarokk; if neither possible, may play any card. Trick won by highest tarokk in it, or by highest card of suit led if no tarokk.
Declarer calls a partner by naming a tarokk (usually the XX); its holder is declarer's partner; the other two are opponents.
Bidding (ascending): three, two, one, solo. To bid you must hold at least one honour (except fourth player after three passes).
Six cards form the talon; declarer and others draw then discard the same number; honours and kings cannot be discarded.
Game is won by the side that takes at least 48 of 94 card points.
Bonuses (trull, four kings, pagátultimó, XXI-catch, centrum, small/large bird, pagátuhu, king ultimó/uhu) can be announced; six Illustrated bonuses score only if announced.
Kontra and rekontra double the score for the game or for an announced bonus.
Player to dealer's right leads to the first trick; winner of each trick leads to the next.

strategy.basic: Bonuses are worth more than the game. If you have the Skíz, your primary mission is to hunt for your opponent's XXI. If you have the XXI, you MUST avoid being caught by the Skíz.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Uhu' setup: If you can't save your Pagát for the last trick, try to use it to win the 8th trick (Uhu). This requires very precise card counting to ensure no higher trumps are left.
strategy.advanced: Bidding Signals: Players use advanced bids to signal whether they can support a 'Pagát Ultimó' or if they are vulnerable to a 'XXI-Catch'.
tips: An announced XXI-Catch is the most dramatic play in the game. Only announce it if you have the Skíz and several middle trumps to force the XXI out.
Protect your partner's King if they announce 'King Ultimó' by leading that suit.

difficulty.hard: Extreme strategic depth; calculates the exact probability of an opponent's XXI being caught; manages multiple simultaneous bonus contracts perfectly.

engine.deckDescription: A 42-card Industrie und Glück tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Skus and 20 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace.
engine.suitDescription: Spades and Clubs are the black suits; Hearts and Diamonds are the red suits. Each colour group keeps only five suited cards.
engine.rankDescription: Each suit contains King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, and one pip card. The black suits keep 10; the red suits keep Ace. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Skus.
